text: A well-designed REST API makes life easier for both developers and users. When creating endpoints, always use clear, logical names that represent resources, such as `/users` or `/orders`. It is equally important to return the correct HTTP status codes—for example, `200 OK` for a successful request, `404 Not Found` for a missing resource, and `400 Bad Request` for invalid input. This helps developers quickly diagnose problems. Furthermore, never skip documentation; good documentation with examples and parameter descriptions saves hours of confusion. Finally, practice versioning, such as `/v1/users`, so you can introduce new features without breaking existing integrations. Consistency and simplicity are the keys to a robust API.
